content.text: The Quay

The harbour lay quiet under a low sky, and nothing moved except the gulls that argued over the nets. By evening the wind had changed, bringing the smell of rain and tar and something older that she could not name.

She had walked the length of the quay twice before admitting that the letter in her pocket would not read itself. He laughed, a short dry sound, and said that in his experience maps were only opinions drawn with a steady hand.

By evening the wind had changed, bringing the smell of rain and tar and something older that she could not name. They ate in silence, the lamp hissing between them, while the clock on the wall lost another minute to its own slowness.

He laughed, a short dry sound, and said that in his experience maps were only opinions drawn with a steady hand. The harbour lay quiet under a low sky, and nothing moved except the gulls that argued over the nets.
